es: Contar una anécdota de infancia combinando una conducta típica con would, un hecho anterior con had been + -ing y el clímax en presente histórico.

teaching.en: In my childhood, I would climb the old tree in our garden every afternoon.
teaching.es: En mi infancia, yo trepaba cada tarde al viejo árbol de nuestro jardín.
teaching.explanationEs: Would + verbo base: la costumbre de la escena, en pasado.
segments: In my childhood, I would climb the
old tree in our garden every afternoon.
teaching.audioText: In my childhood, I would climb the old tree in our garden every afternoon.

teaching.en: I had been climbing for ten minutes when I reached the highest branch.
teaching.es: Llevaba diez minutos trepando cuando llegué a la rama más alta.
teaching.explanationEs: Had been + -ing con for: la actividad en curso antes del hecho clave.
segments: I had been climbing for ten minutes
when I reached the highest branch.
teaching.audioText: I had been climbing for ten minutes when I reached the highest branch.

teaching.en: So there I am, on the branch, and I hear a loud noise!
teaching.es: Y ahí estoy yo, en la rama, ¡y oigo un ruido fuerte!
teaching.explanationEs: Presente histórico para el clímax, con la señal «So there I am».
segments: So there I am, on the branch,
and I hear a loud noise!
teaching.audioText: So there I am, on the branch, and I hear a loud noise!

teaching.en: I am terrified, I hold on tight, and Dad runs to get a ladder.
teaching.es: Estoy aterrorizado, me agarro fuerte y papá corre a buscar una escalera.
teaching.explanationEs: Varios presentes seguidos hacen el clímax rápido.
segments: I am terrified, I hold on tight,
and Dad runs to get a ladder.
teaching.audioText: I am terrified, I hold on tight, and Dad runs to get a ladder.

teaching.en: The rescue took ten minutes, and I never climbed that tree again.
teaching.es: El rescate duró diez minutos y nunca volví a subir a ese árbol.
teaching.explanationEs: Vuelta al pasado simple para el final; again va al final de la frase.
segments: The rescue took ten minutes, and
I never climbed that tree again.
teaching.audioText: The rescue took ten minutes, and I never climbed that tree again.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cuenta lo que hacías cada verano de niño?

choices.text: Yesterday I played in the river.
Every summer I would play in the river.
Now I am playing in the river.

feedback.es: Would + verbo base, con un marcador como every summer, cuenta una costumbre de la infancia.

hint.es: Busca would + verbo base y un marcador de costumbre.

prompt.es: Completa: «Llevaba una hora esperando cuando empezó a llover.»

feedback.es: Had been + verbo en -ing presenta la actividad en curso antes del hecho clave: had been waiting.

origin.text: I had been ___ for an hour when it started to rain.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas frases funciona como clímax de la historia?

choices.text: Last night I was at home and it was dark.
I had been sitting there for an hour.
So there I am, in the dark, and the door opens slowly!

feedback.es: El clímax pide presente histórico y una señal («So there I am»); las otras dos preparan la escena y el antecedente.

hint.es: El clímax va en presente histórico.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nunca volví a ver a ese perro.»

answer.text: I never saw that dog again

feedback.es: Again va al final: never saw that dog again.

prompt.es: Completa: «De pronto mi hermano abre la puerta y grita.»

feedback.es: En el clímax, los verbos van en presente histórico: opens y shouts.

origin.text: Suddenly my brother ___ the door and shouts.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su parte de la anécdota.

pairs: Every Saturday we would play football in the street.
We had been playing for an hour when it got dark.
So there I am, alone, and the lights go out!
Afterwards, we all went home and laughed.

feedback.es: Cada parte usa su tiempo: would para la costumbre, had been + -ing para el antecedente, presente para el clímax y pasado para el final.

pairs: Every Saturday we would play football in the street.
We had been playing for an hour when it got dark.
So there I am, alone, and the lights go out!
Afterwards, we all went home and laughed.

prompt.es: En el relato, ¿qué frase es el antecedente del hecho clave?

choices.text: We had been skating for two hours when the lights went out.
Every winter my cousins and I would go skating.
So there we are, in the dark!

feedback.es: Had been + -ing + for presenta lo que llevaban haciendo antes de que se fuera la luz; la primera frase es la costumbre y la tercera, el clímax.

origin.text: Every winter my cousins and I would go skating. One evening we had been skating for two hours when the lights went out. So there we are, in the dark! Afterwards we walked home, laughing.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hacía Sara de pequeña.

choices.text: She played there only one morning.
She regularly played there in the morning.

feedback.es: Would + verbo base, con when she was a child, cuenta una costumbre repetida de su infancia.

origin.audio: When Sara was a child, she would play in the park every morning.

prompt.es: Completa: «Llevábamos dos horas caminando cuando empezó a llover.»

feedback.es: Para medir cuánto duraba la actividad se usa for + tiempo, no since.

origin.text: We had been walking ___ two hours when it started to rain.

prompt.es: Escribe tu anécdota de infancia, de 55 a 110 palabras.

answer.text: When I was a child, I would ride my bike in the park every afternoon. One day I had been riding for half an hour when I heard a loud noise. So there I am, in the middle of the path, and a big dog runs towards me! I am terrified, and I shout for help. Suddenly my dad arrives and calls the dog. Afterwards, I never went to the park alone again.
accepted: When I was a child, I would ride my bike in the park every afternoon. One day I had been riding for half an hour when I heard a loud noise. So there I am, in the middle of the path, and a big dog runs towards me! I am terrified, and I shout for help. Suddenly my dad arrives and calls the dog. Afterwards, I never went to the park alone again.

As a child, I would cycle in the park every afternoon. One day I had been cycling for half an hour when I heard a noise. So there I am, on the path, and a big dog comes towards me! I am scared and I shout. Suddenly my father arrives and calls the dog. After that, I never went to the park alone again.

feedback.es: La anécdota necesita las cuatro partes: costumbre con would, antecedente con had been + -ing, clímax en presente histórico y final en pasado.

origin.text: Datos: cada tarde montabas en bici por el parque (costumbre). Un día llevabas media hora montando cuando oíste un ruido (antecedente). Clímax: un perro grande corre hacia ti, tienes miedo y gritas. Final: tu padre llama al perro y nunca volviste a ir solo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es el final correcto, en pasado?

choices.text: So there we are, and we never play again.
We would never play in that street tomorrow.
Afterwards, we never played in that street again.

feedback.es: El final vuelve al pasado simple y lleva again al final de la frase; las otras dos mezclan el presente o el futuro.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada tarde hacía los deberes en el jardín.»

feedback.es: Do my homework es una acción repetida del pasado: would + verbo base cuenta la costumbre.

origin.text: Every afternoon I ___ do my homework in the garden.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Llevaba tres horas estudiando cuando se fue la luz.»

answer.text: I had been studying for three hours when the light went out

feedback.es: Had been studying + for three hours presenta la actividad anterior al hecho clave.
